claims.wording: Reclaim offers Caches, Downloads, Languages, Logs and Trash categories, a Safe/Aggressive criteria slider, and result inspection before Clean.

claims.wording: Duplicates analyzes actual file data and offers location selection, selection rules, Finder reveal and Quick Look before Clean.

claims.conditions: Advanced preferences offer moving duplicates to Trash instead of permanent deletion; not a blanket Trash guarantee for Reclaim.

claims.wording: Organize addresses Desktop, Dock and Smart Folders.

claims.conditions: Organization is not synonymous with reclaiming storage or uninstalling an app.

article.title: Review duplicate copies before reclaiming space on a Mac
article.intent: Separate duplicate-copy decisions from cache cleanup and Desktop organization, using Washing Machine X9's documented cycles.
outline: Pick a cleanup job before selecting files
Compare duplicate locations and preview the copy you intend to keep
Check the duplicates-to-Trash preference; do not assume Reclaim is reversible
Treat Dock/Desktop organization as a different task
Choose a storage investigation workflow when the problem is unexplained growth
article.interactionPass: A non-destructive decision checklist: original backed up, copy location understood, preview checked, deletion method known, rebuild/download cost accepted. No live filesystem controls.

article.boundary: Documented workflow, not a hands-on tutorial, benchmark or claim that Breathing Room replaces duplicate detection.
